description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/each.t:319-330).

The rows:

    use feature 'refaliasing'; no warnings 'experimental::refaliasing';
    $a = 7;  my %h2;  \$h2{f} = \$a;  ($a, $b) = (each %h2);
    is "$a $b", "f 7", 'each in list assignment';        # PCL: " 7"
    ...  ($c, $d) = (values %h3);
    is "$c $d", "3 7", 'values in list assignment';      # PCL: " 7"

MEASURED, and this is the finding: the same code IN ISOLATION agrees with
perl 5.40.3 exactly (probes/p9.pl rows 6-8 -- `each` after a refalias gives
`f 7`, `values` gives `3 `, a plain `each` gives `k 9`; PCL byte for byte the
same as perl on all three).  So the divergence inside `t/op/each.t` is
DOWNSTREAM STATE of the file, in the s473t6a sense ("a row that agrees in
isolation is downstream state and the cause must say so"), and it is NOT
isolated further here.

What the file does before these rows that the probe does not: it runs 63
earlier rows including the Unicode-key block whose keys COLLIDE under PCL
(the file's rows 35/36/38, `NS:Unicode semantics differences` in this same
pass), a `keys`-assignment block, and `%ENV` iteration.  `$a`/`$b` are the
sort globals and are written by earlier `sort` calls in the file.

NEXT STEP when this is picked up: bisect the file rather than the statement --
run `t/op/each.t` with the blocks before line 319 removed one at a time until
the two rows agree, and only then write a mechanism.  Do NOT assume `each`,
the refalias or the list assignment: all three are measured innocent on their
own.
